title: Beta-Resorcylaldehyde attenuates DSS-induced colitis by inhibiting inflammation and oxidative stress through the Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1 pathway.
authors: Xiang, Lei; Yang, Xue; Li, Qingzhou; Wang, Guilin; Hu, Rui; Li, Mingrui; Hu, Jushan; Lei, Haoran; Fan, Anran; Gong, Zipeng; Wang, Dong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究BRAL通过Keap1/Nrf2/HO-1通路缓解结肠炎，虽涉及分子对接和MD模拟，但核心是蛋白-小分子互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，与TF-DNA课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ulcerative colitis (UC), a bowel condition marked by heightened oxidative stress, ongoing inflammation, and intestinal barrier dysfunction, has limited therapeutic options that are both effective and safe. AIM: This study evaluated the therapeutic impacts and mechanisms of beta-Resorcylaldehyde (BRAL), the natural phenolic aldehyde derived from Morus alba wood, on dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced UC. METHODS: A murine DSS-induced UC model was employed to assess the therapeutic effects of BRAL by assessing disease activity, histopathology, oxidative stress, cytokine expression, and intestinal barrier integrity in vivo. To investigate the underlying molecular mechanisms, RNA sequencing, quantitative PCR, and Western blot experiments were conducted. For in vitro validation, RAW264.7 macrophages and THP-1 cells stimulated with lipopolysaccharide and intestinal epithelial cells injured by tert-butyl hydroperoxide were utilized. The assessment of target engagement was carried out using the cellular thermal shift assay, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation. RESULTS: BRAL markedly alleviated the symptoms of DSS-induced UC, reduced oxidative stress and inflammatory reactions, along with restored tight junction protein expression. Transcriptomic and biochemical analyses indicated that BRAL suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine production while enhancing antioxidant defenses. Mechanistically, BRAL directly bound to Keap1, thereby promoting Nrf2 nuclear translocation and Nrf2/HO-1 pathway activation. Notably, pharmacological inhibition of Nrf2 with the well-known inhibitor ML385 abolished the protective effects of BRAL. CONCLUSION: BRAL improves DSS-induced UC through targeting Keap1 to activate Nrf2 signaling, thereby restoring redox homeostasis, suppressing inflammation, and preserving epithelial barrier integrity. These findings suggest that BRAL is a promising natural candidate for treating UC.
abstract_zh: 背景：溃疡性结肠炎（UC）是一种以氧化应激增强、持续炎症和肠道屏障功能障碍为特征的肠道疾病，目前有效且安全的治疗选择有限。目的：本研究评估了β-间苯二酚醛（BRAL）——一种源自桑木的天然酚醛——对葡聚糖硫酸钠（DSS）诱导的UC的治疗效果及其机制。方法：采用小鼠DSS诱导的UC模型，通过评估疾病活动度、组织病理学、氧化应激、细胞因子表达和体内肠道屏障完整性来评价BRAL的治疗效果。为探究潜在分子机制，进行了RNA测序、定量PCR和Western blot实验。体外验证中，使用了脂多糖刺激的RAW264.7巨噬细胞和THP-1细胞，以及叔丁基过氧化氢损伤的肠道上皮细胞。靶点结合评估通过细胞热位移分析、分子对接和分子动力学模拟进行。结果：BRAL显著缓解了DSS诱导的UC症状，降低了氧化应激和炎症反应，并恢复了紧密连接蛋白的表达。转录组学和生化分析表明，BRAL抑制了促炎细胞因子的产生，同时增强了抗氧化防御能力。机制上，BRAL直接结合Keap1，从而促进Nrf2核转位和Nrf2/HO-1通路激活。值得注意的是，使用已知抑制剂ML385对Nrf2进行药理学抑制后，BRAL的保护作用被消除。结论：BRAL通过靶向Keap1激活Nrf2信号通路，从而恢复氧化还原稳态、抑制炎症并维持上皮屏障完整性，从而改善DSS诱导的UC。这些发现表明，BRAL是治疗UC的有前景的天然候选药物。
